_comment: Seed grammar constructions (controller §8: 2–3). Three patterns, each one the
seed sentences and the integration passage actually use — a construction with no
attested use in the dataset would be a claim the seed cannot support.
Explanations and examples are original text written for this project; they are not
quoted or adapted from any grammar reference.

records.name: split into ~
records.explanation: [Noun]に分かれる states the result of a division: what stands before に is what the subject ends up as — a count of parts (二つ), or named branches (上りと下り). The verb is intransitive, so the thing divides and no agent is named. 分ける is its transitive partner: 道を二つに分ける is someone dividing the road, 道が二つに分かれる is the road forking.
records.example: 線路は二つに分かれる。
records.exampleTranslation: The railway line splits in two.

records.name: whether or not ~
records.explanation: [Plain form]かどうか embeds a yes/no question inside a larger sentence. It attaches to the plain form of verbs and i-adjectives; a noun or na-adjective drops だ before it (学生だ → 学生かどうか). Do not use かどうか when a question word is already present — どの道を行くか, not どの道を行くかどうか — because かどうか supplies the missing yes/no alternative that a question word has already filled.
records.example: その道が駅まで続くかどうか分からない。
records.exampleTranslation: I don't know whether that road continues as far as the station.

records.name: decide to ~
records.explanation: [Plain non-past verb]ことにする reports a decision the speaker made themselves. The past 〜ことにした is the ordinary way to announce a decision already taken. Contrast 〜ことになる, which reports an outcome that arrived without the speaker choosing it: 行くことにした is 'I decided to go', 行くことになった is 'it was decided that I go'.
records.example: 右の道を行くことにした。
records.exampleTranslation: I decided to take the road on the right.
